reviews.text: 很幽默的一款游戏，莫名其妙戳中了我的笑点，有时候是被自己气笑的有时候是被对手蠢笑的，以及观众真的喜欢看我在棋盘上跑马拉松浪费时间、大口喝血或者拿着网子不停扔小蜘蛛吗？总之，所有人都很好笑（尤其是对面的刺客哥一个飞跃创死自己的队友的同时打爆旁边汽油桶把自己崩个半死最后跪在地上要加入我的时候）
战棋版本的暗黑地牢1，简约不简单。 序章：“我的家族没落了~”…… 第一章：喜刷刷喜刷刷喜刷刷 第二章：遍地陷阱和地形杀感觉在玩扫雷 第三章：堆怪堆地形太严重了，过多的场外要素玩着反而累赘不得劲，变成了无聊的重复劳动。 然后就懒得再玩了，总的来说高开低走，新鲜劲过了就没啥意思了，终究达不到暗黑地牢的高度。中评吧。
窗口化长时间放置之后程序未响应
荣耀之路这个任务成就显示已完结，但是实际任务栏里面还是一直存在，应该是bug
在竞技场的老路上，我们都获得了救赎... chapter one：ruin has come to our family...
请立刻增加瑟瑟内容！
我不知道是我自己衰还是有什么我不了解的制作机制，玩过好些游戏测试版和正式版明明差不多的内容，测试版丝滑流畅，正式版就总出bug。这个游戏也是，demo一点毛病没有，正式版就会出现无法正确加载，我还怀疑是不是旧存档的问题重新开了新档，但是就经常加载完了只显示背景不显示界面的文字，有时候背景都不是正常流程中的背景，是建筑已经点满的背景。

我真的想给差评的是，为什么新版出来了一个城镇事件，事件惩罚特别重，这能玩下去吗？为什么事件决策不是有好有坏？居然能出现两个同时负面的选择，一个全体角斗士获得流血+撕裂，一个医护所关闭？就没了。一个正面效果都没有。 我真不知道这种设计是为了什么，差评！ -------------------------------- 12.1 虽然负面事件改了，但是设计师你能告诉玩家你们设计的技能有什么用处？除了拉人的技能有点用，别的技能意义太低，要么打得太短，伤害又没多少 ---------------------------------- 3.23 技能到底有什么用处？？不要说成长性，升级扩大范围就是有问题，一开始看不到好的，要升级才好用。。这算什么，升级加加数值得了，连形态都发生变化了，1级技能根本找不到用处，那我升级干嘛？

数值屌差。有太多毛病，目前不建议入手。 先说优点，本身的底层思路很好。类暗黑地牢的经营和角色培养。战斗又是回合制战旗。各个职业技能虽说有很多毛病（这个等等说），但至少做到了各个职业差别很大，各具特色。 缺点很多，很多。 1、技能，可能是为了低等级和高等级有差距，导致许多低等级技能阉割十分严重，以至于不能玩，点名批评游侠的所有召唤系技能鸡肋，前期看到都不想收。问题是，如果低技能做不到有用，如何引导玩家培养低等级角色？做了，但是玩家不想体验，这是很大的败笔。低等级技能需要加强让玩家提得起兴趣去用，而且需要一个百科来说明不同等级技能的效果，而不是让玩家只能在有这个技能并且能升级的时候，才能看到下一级的效果。 2、装备，目前装备就是纯数值，没有机制，很粗糙。以至于当玩家体验了第一章的新鲜感以后，唯一的新鲜感来源只有新敌人。而且，我很需要一键脱下所有角色装备。角色装备槽位比暗黑地牢多很多，而装备本身又是纯数值，导致下本之前穿装备变成纯垃圾时间。 3、回家事件，纯败笔。目前来看，我没遇到任何一件有正面收益的。动不动就全体上永久伤，强行拖慢节奏打乱我计划；动不动就扣30%的金币，导致我根本不敢存钱；动不动就关停我的设施，然后给个几百块打发我；动不动就改我手下的特质，本来好好的C位拿个增伤特质，给我改成乱七八糟的特质； 目前玩到第二章，感觉玩不下去了。游戏距离能玩还有很远的距离。想玩想买的，建议等一年以后再看看

没悔棋，没有难度选择，自动存档会覆盖旧的存档对新手不太友好，一不小心存档就玩坏了。 各种功能是逐步解锁的，算是照顾新手方便学习。 No undo moves, no difficulty selection, and auto-saving overwrites old saves — not very beginner-friendly, as a single misstep can ruin your progress. Features are unlocked gradually, which helps newcomers learn the game step by step.

法师的地块效果存在只有三个回合然而这个游戏的角色每个人的回合结束都会推动环境回合，结合这个游戏卡得要死的走位和技能范围，我的法师能够打到的往往只有上一个朝他走来且刚好停在他面前的敌人，而那个可笑的环境效果根本没法持续到那个敌人的回合就会因为自己和其他敌人的回合的流逝消失，那我这个职业他的地块效果有什么存在的意义吗？还有敌人强化效果设计师真的自己测试过吗？我不特意速杀就会给我叠到根本打不动的状态这是对的吗？这游戏设计上左右脑互搏的程度让我感觉像是在玩一个精神分裂患者的杰作。

首先这款游戏的题材很新颖，角斗场类的战棋游戏，应该说没有同类竞品，光是这点就足够我入坑这款游戏了。 而另一方面，这款游戏确实体验了角斗场的残酷，角色死亡就没了，不管培养的多厉害，还有很多负面的事件等影响玩家体验。 很多人说这些很搞心态，所以打差评。但是我说一句，既然你都准备体验角斗场的残酷了，你还想游戏给你很轻松的游戏氛围，那你就不适合玩这类游戏。 总的来说虽然这游戏标注的还是体验版，但实际完成度已经很高了，唯一需要做的就是根据反馈平衡游戏中的各方面，但总得来说并不影响目前的游戏体验，对于我个人而言，还是很喜欢和看好这款游戏的！

玩了然后退款了 说是缝了最后的咒语和暗黑地牢，可惜缝了个皮毛，有其型无其实 首先最后的咒语里，装备词条、人物属性词条、特性、天赋树等。 光是拿装备来说，不同武器不同技能树，不限定职业，一人可带两套武器，还有头盔、衣服、裤子、两个饰品，高级装备5、6个额外词条等等，这里的深度就已经不是多了一星半点。 然后是人物属性，行动点、移动力、生命值、法力值、护甲、减伤、闪避、暴击、暴击伤害；远程攻击强度、物理攻击强度、魔法攻击强度、各种回复效率、获取效率、几率；连击、蔓延、禁锢、眩晕、中毒、流血、目盲，各种buff、debuff机制；这里所有的属性能被装备、天赋、特性影响，角斗士的这些设计真的是寒酸啊。 然后是战斗，最蠢的一点是角斗士不能斜对角攻击，队友有阻挡不能穿越，再加上那可悲的3点移动力，还有只能打直线的远程弹道。这也是太有特色了。 然后是暗黑地牢，下一趟迷宫死2个疯3个，脑袋挂裤腰带上战战兢兢、步履维艰，到后面熟悉了机制熟悉了人物，慢慢打得游刃有余最后追求极限，跟黑魂似的在折磨中成长的酣畅淋漓。而角斗士的战斗呢，真的是太过平淡了。 平淡无味的79块钱，不如买顿肯德基吃的爽

这游戏让我上头！本来只想“再来一回合”，结果天亮了。我的角斗士在场上浴血奋战，我在屏幕前和观众一起狂欢，这像素风搭配四溅的血浆，莫名带感。 游戏完美诠释了“既要赢，更要赢得漂亮”。观众就是一群“甲方爸爸”，随时给你丢任务：用陷阱杀两个、秀个特定技能……满足了他们，奖励拿到手软。每次击败敌方明星角斗士，拇指朝上还是朝下全凭你一念之间，是收编他还是扒他装备，这抉择太酸爽了。 虽然永久死亡机制让我几次痛失爱将，恨不得砸键盘，但那种“贪生怕死就富不了”的博弈实在让人欲罢不能。如果你喜欢在刀尖上跳舞，顺便体验一把当角斗士老板的滋味，这游戏绝对值回票价！

Bloodgrounds… what can I say? You almost get the impression that you’re playing The Last Spell. The game feels sluggish, simply because there is no music during combat. The artistic style is genuinely successful, the builds are varied, and the different consumables (scrolls, traps, potions, etc.) are relevant and well thought out. The equipment allows for a wide variety of very interesting setups. However, the game’s sound design lacks impact. This is a gladiator game, so you would expect a brutal sound design that pays homage to the gladiator universe. Unfortunately, this is not the case: the sound design feels cheap and far too timid. The game also suffers from a serious lack of readability, especially in combat. The timeline at the top is barely understandable, and your gladiators’ portraits are displayed almost in the same color as those of the enemies, whereas it would have made sense to give them a clearly different color to distinguish them properly in the timeline. I particularly like this arena mechanic with debuffs and obstacles that attack periodically. But once again, the lack of “readability” makes it difficult to clearly tell what is dangerous and what is not. In short, there are many other issues, and I don’t really feel like dwelling on listing them all. There is still a lot of work to be done on this game, and it only took me 2 hours of playtime to already notice no fewer than 5 or 6 glaring problems. I do not recommend it in its current state, but the game will fully realize its potential once it is finished. [h2] Edit [/h2] Nothing has changed with version 1.0. Sure, there are more activities and more freedom, like weapon crafting, but the sound design is still a huge joke. When a spiked mace hit sounds the same as a frying pan recorded with a microphone bought on TEMU, there’s clearly a real coherence problem. The sound design and the readability of Bloodgrounds are by far the two least successful elements, by a wide margin. Everything else is successful and I want to be very clear about that, but I’d honestly be willing to chip in to a fundraiser (if it’s a budget issue) to help the dev team give us a real sound design worthy of the game, because right now it’s a complete disaster

[h1]这是一个能让玩家伤心欲绝的游戏！[/h1] 回合制策略战棋游戏玩过不少，但是角色在战斗过程中死亡就永久死亡的，还真的是不多，一般这种模式都会出现在可选择的“铁血模式”、“硬核模式”之类模式里的，如同《Bloodgrounds》（《角斗士血域》）这样在普通模式下都这样的，实在是少见。（分分钟是俺孤陋寡闻也说不定的） [h1][quote=] [table] [tr] [th] 欢迎关注 [b][u][i]U_U鉴赏家培养计划[/i][/u][/b][/th] [/tr] [tr] [th] 关注U_U鉴赏家，开启精彩游戏之旅。 [/th] [/tr] [/table] [/quote][/h1] [h1]简单粗暴了剧情[/h1] 在《角斗士血域》里，我们在最后的角斗士战场里凯旋，成为荣归故里的“传奇”，也因此决定在故乡建设角斗士训练场，开始招募并训练新的角斗士，让他们也一步步踏上残酷的角斗场，最终直面有杀父之仇的暴君！ [h1]直接明了的玩法搭配永久性死亡的设定[/h1] 游戏的玩法其实挺简单，就是建设基地、招募具有各种技能和属性的角斗士、给他们安排各种训练和配备各种装备，然后安排他们踏上角斗场决一死战。但这里有一个相当有意思的机制，那就是无论我们倾注多少心血、配备多少神装的角斗士，他只要在角斗场上战败，那就是真正的挂掉了！身上的各种神装也无法拿回来，再次见到他就只能是在基地的“墓园”里了！因此在战斗的时候就需要格外注意了。 [h1]更有意思的策略战棋战斗[/h1] 《角斗士血域》作为一款回合制策略战棋游戏，最为重要的当然是战斗系统，游戏里我们和敌方的角斗士都只能在比较简单的方正网格战场上战斗，战场上会有一些柱子和陷阱作为阻碍，时不时观众席还会扔下各种祝福什么的，可以用来回血或者提升角色状态。我们的角斗士需要根据各自的行动点和技能点来行动，只要有剩余，就能多次操作。对了，想要获得更好的战斗奖励，每局战斗的“观众任务”还是得认真完成，除了基本的金币、经验和装备奖励外，时不时还会有一些永久的属性提升奖励的，可遇不可求的同时，也是让战斗增加更多的挑战乐趣的。 [h1]有一定随机元素的角色养成[/h1] 游戏里每个角斗士都有自己的职业、天赋和技能，还都能进行升级养成，除了装备各种各样不同的装备之外，技能的调整搭配也是提升实力的主要途径。有意思的是，角色升级的时候，我们手动给他们提升的时候，是需要随机肉鸽三选一的，至于是出现什么等阶的属性（普通、稀有、史诗等等阶），那是全看天命！当然，也可以使用金币进行刷新，但那代价是真不低！也因此想要培养出一个符合心意的高手出来，除了需要花费时间、心血之外，还需要一定的运气的！也因此如果角斗士不小心挂了，那是真的会心疼到拍键盘摔鼠标的！ [h1]略微简略的基地建设玩法[/h1] 《角斗士血域》虽然也有着基地建设的玩法，但较为简略，就是那么几座简单的建筑，功能也较为单一，酒馆是用来招募新角斗士的、学院是用来训练新技能的、市场是用来买装备的、墓园是用来缅怀战死的手下的、医护所是用来给手下治疗回血的等等，虽说各建筑能升级，但整体的功能就这么些个，对比于同类竞品游戏来说，还是单调了点的。 [h1]贵是贵了点，但真的好玩！[/h1] 整体而言，《角斗士血域》虽说画风有点古老，但玩法和创意也算是有特色的，无论是永久死亡机制，还是观众任务系统，都是需要我们在战斗里花费更多的时间来制定策略，这也更好的契合策略战棋游戏的玩法初衷，反正喜欢战棋游戏的小伙伴千万不要错过就对了！（虽说这游戏丫的还真的是贵了点，等打折吧！）

I had a blast with this game all through the first act. Then i got to the 2nd act and the map traps went nuts. Its too much. I cant even move my Gladiators a single square. I don't mind the challenge its just annoying and to me takes the fun out of it.

体量太小了，无论是基地建设还是角斗士养成深度都不够，几个章节都是刷挑战重复度太高，本身回合制就墨迹，为了提升战斗的趣味性加一堆战场机制导致战斗更加的墨迹。基地建设没有什么特殊收集要素，就是过剧情解锁升级，很无趣。不同的职业也没什么区分，没有专属装备，什么装备都能混着穿，法师能穿重甲当血牛，战士反而只能近战很尴尬。关键剧情过于平淡，前几章都没有什么有记忆的剧情点，导致过剧情就是单纯的刷竞技场，很无聊，皇帝的最终战也没有什么特别的机制，而且最终章还有BUG，商店什么都不卖。除了美术风格还可以以外，其他的游戏内容不值这个价，想玩的建议等五折以上的大折扣再入手。

数值和平衡性屌差，我第一次见到有借机攻击是按照百分比扣血的，你一个重甲战士从战士还是弓箭手法师面前走开被借机都是掉一样的血，这合理吗？像那个投网的技能，没伤害还要两费，纯垃圾技能，很多技能打半天没有平A高，回血就回个位数，连战多得离谱还有各种必须去医院才能恢复的debuff，越打越难打。而且角斗士打输了也不是必死的啊，也要看观众觉得打得好不好决定能活下来，有时候一场战斗本来打得很好，最后脆皮突然被一顿集火死了，特别是人物还要反复刷图才能成长，死了什么都得不到装备还要没收，挫败感极强。 还有我不知道为什么战斗力途中不能存档或中断，而且移动后不能取消，连战又特别长有六七场战斗，一个操作错误就走错可能导致全灭，等于半小时白打，真无语。

Most of the negative reviews here seem to come from skill issues. The game has plenty of depth and playability if you aren't A) bad, B) intentionally cheesing the easiest possible route to avoid mechanics Worth the price, fun game for it's genre with improvements coming steadily

给开发者提些建议： 1.正式版1.0出来后，虽然增加了观众情绪系统，但是观众任务依然单调，+暴击伤害、+先攻是少数能提升属性的任务，但更多任务的收益与付出不成正比。尤其是通关后继续刷的玩家，很容易丧失游玩兴趣。 2.新增加的武器锻造系统，传说装备打造的几率极低，我试过锻造40多件轻甲手部都不出传说的情况（最高锻造花费），这还不说实际上很多紫装属性词条都要比传说装备好得多。 3.其实跟上一条相关，就是关于传说装备的属性词条，经常出现“承伤、金币获取、经验获取、幸运率、闪避率”这种增益效果较低的词条，远不如紫装。可是等商店能刷到或者自己能锻造传说装备，已经接近后期游戏结束了，这个时候如果传说装备还总是出现这样鸡肋的词条，让传说装备和通关后还继续刷的玩家失去了意义。 4.实测发现，如果连续2次远征任务失败后会损失50%或者75%，会直接导致角斗士死亡，我认为开发者应该对此作出提示。 5.战斗开场布置占位时需要使用到鼠标中键，但有些玩家鼠标是没有中键功能的，而键位设置中又没有改键功能。
体量不大，难度不高，提升空间不小。

Glad there is an option for increased combat speed, so I could realize how grindy and unbalanced it is. Surely some Redditor will say something like "durr skill issue," and that’s fine. If you enjoy replaying the same mundane fights, utilizing mostly the same tactics to circumvent the game's many tedious mechanics—until you can repeat this same boring loop with slightly higher numbers—then go for it.

I spend too much time trying to find the game that scratches that itch for me. I found it. This game perfectly blends TBT, RPG elements, camp management and stress free fun. Thanks Devs! I hope more content is coming our way!

[h1][b]6/10[/b][/h1] Bloodgrounds is a decent turn-based strategy & management game with a relatively unique gladiator vibe. The gladiator stuff really makes the game special. Usually, you fight a series of battles and have to manage your resources and health such that you can make it to the boss and actually kill them. And the boss fights are rather challenging. Then you go back to town and upgrade buildings, manage/train gladiators, buy stuff, heal, etc. And repeat. What killed it for me was tons of anti-synergy in my favorite class, and the fact I couldn't turn up the difficulty: it got too easy after 10 hours and I had no reason to play anymore :( [h2]Pros:[/h2] - Visually appealing overall, nice pixel graphics - Everything seems very intuitive - Audience Quests are *really* cool. Love this mechanic so much as it fits the gladiator vibe perfectly (if you fulfill the requirements during battle, you get extra rewards). Also there's an Audience Meter and if you please the audience you get more loot - You don't have to spend several turns moving to get close enough to attack - It's rather gory - Boss fights are pretty challenging & have different music. They're very fun [h2]Mehs:[/h2] - The whole game is a bit monochromatic with all the sand-colored everything but I suppose it does help create contrast for the icons, health/move/AP bars, abilities, etc - Ok music & sound design though it's a bit thin and repetitive [h2]Cons:[/h2] - No text or UI scaling. It's just a little too small - There's no way to delay your turn? Disappointing - Lots of anti-synergy for many classes, like how Magus weapons all cause Burn but their cold abilities cancel Burn. Or how they can only apply Frost with abilities that put them next to an enemy but then can't attack with any weapons there - Can't change difficulty and the game get easier as you go. So you either suffer early on with a higher difficulty or the game becomes too easy. Dev told me people would abuse it if it could be changed but I don't see why that matters in a single player game Just for reference, I'm finding that gladiators with the 50% chance of an extra AP on kill are especially useful. Despite anti-synergies, Magus class is fantastic for the teleport and the ability to use staffs (ranged weapon that doesn't require LoS or being in a straight line). They're limited on what abilities are actually useful but the teleport is just amazing.

Bloodgrounds is a tactical strategy title developed by Exordium Games and published by Daedalic Entertainment. The game blends several gameplay systems—turn-based tactics, roguelite progression, RPG-style character development, and city management—into a brutal arena-focused experience centered around gladiatorial combat. Set in a dark fantasy world inspired by ancient arenas and mythological influences, Bloodgrounds places players in the role of a former gladiator who has escaped slavery and risen to become a powerful patron controlling their own stable of fighters. From this new position, the player must recruit warriors, manage resources, and guide a growing team of gladiators through deadly tournaments with the ultimate goal of exacting revenge on the emperor responsible for their past suffering. The narrative foundation of Bloodgrounds revolves around this personal quest for vengeance. The protagonist was once forced to fight for survival in the arenas of the empire, enduring countless battles under the rule of a cruel regime that treats gladiators as disposable entertainment. After gaining freedom and wealth, the protagonist returns to the world of arena combat not as a fighter but as a strategist and organizer. By building a powerful organization of gladiators and competing in tournaments across the land, the player gradually rises through the ranks of the empire’s blood sport hierarchy. The ultimate objective is to reach the grand arenas of the imperial capital and confront the tyrant who once controlled their fate. While the storyline serves primarily as a framework for the gameplay, it successfully establishes a grim atmosphere filled with political intrigue, corrupt nobles, and a society built on violent spectacle. Combat forms the core of the gameplay experience and takes place in turn-based tactical battles on grid-based arenas. Each gladiator under the player’s command possesses unique abilities, equipment, and combat roles that determine how they perform in battle. Some fighters excel at direct melee combat, others specialize in ranged attacks or tactical support, and certain characters rely on magical abilities drawn from the game’s mythological elements. Positioning is crucial during battles, as the arenas often contain obstacles, traps, and environmental hazards that can dramatically influence the outcome of a fight. Players must carefully manage action points each turn to move, attack, defend, or activate special abilities, making every decision significant in the flow of combat. One of the most striking aspects of Bloodgrounds is its roguelite-inspired permadeath system. Gladiators who fall in battle are permanently lost, along with their equipment and the experience they accumulated over time. This mechanic introduces a constant sense of tension and risk during every encounter. A single miscalculation can result in the loss of a veteran champion who may have taken hours of gameplay to develop. Because of this, players are constantly forced to balance ambition with caution, deciding whether to pursue risky strategies for greater rewards or protect valuable fighters from unnecessary danger. Surviving gladiators gain experience, unlock new abilities, and acquire stronger equipment, gradually evolving into powerful warriors capable of handling more dangerous opponents. Outside the arena, Bloodgrounds expands into a deeper management system that adds another layer of strategic planning. Players oversee the development of a coastal stronghold known as Marevento, which functions as the headquarters of the gladiatorial organization. Through the construction and upgrading of various buildings, players unlock new opportunities to strengthen their team. Training facilities allow gladiators to learn new abilities, infirmaries heal injuries sustained in battle, and shrines grant blessings from different gods that can influence combat outcomes. Other buildings provide economic advantages, improve equipment crafting, or establish underground contacts capable of sabotaging rival fighters before tournaments begin. The progression system encourages players to constantly refine both their team composition and their strategic approach. As campaigns progress, new enemy types appear with specialized abilities that force players to adapt their tactics. Some opponents rely on overwhelming physical strength, while others use magic, ranged attacks, or support abilities that complicate straightforward combat strategies. This evolving roster of enemies ensures that battles remain unpredictable and challenging throughout the game. Another distinctive feature is the influence of the arena audience. Spectators attending the gladiatorial matches crave excitement and spectacle, rewarding players who perform dramatic and entertaining actions during battles. Executing stylish finishing moves, pushing enemies into traps, or creating visually impressive combat sequences can earn additional rewards and favor from the crowd. This system encourages players to take calculated risks in pursuit of glory, turning each battle into both a tactical challenge and a performance designed to satisfy the bloodthirsty spectators. Visually, Bloodgrounds employs a stylized dark fantasy aesthetic that emphasizes gritty pixel-art environments and dramatic combat animations. The arenas are filled with detailed elements such as spikes, collapsing structures, and environmental hazards that players can exploit during battles. Character designs are varied and expressive, ranging from armored warriors and agile duelists to magical fighters and monstrous enemies inspired by mythological creatures. Despite the intensity of combat, the visual presentation remains clear and readable, ensuring that players can easily track movement, abilities, and enemy positions. The overall pacing of the game benefits from the alternating structure between tactical combat and city management. After surviving a brutal arena battle, players return to their base to recruit new fighters, upgrade facilities, and prepare for the next challenge. This rhythm creates a satisfying gameplay loop where strategic planning and intense combat reinforce each other. Over time, players build a formidable organization capable of competing in larger tournaments and confronting increasingly powerful enemies. However, Bloodgrounds can also be quite unforgiving, particularly during the early stages of a campaign. The combination of permadeath, unpredictable enemy behavior, and occasional random elements means that even experienced players may suffer sudden setbacks. Losing a well-developed gladiator can be frustrating, but it also reinforces the high-stakes nature of the arena. For players who enjoy strategic games where every decision carries weight, this difficulty adds to the sense of tension and accomplishment. Ultimately, Bloodgrounds succeeds in delivering a deep and engaging tactical experience that blends multiple gameplay systems into a cohesive whole. Its combination of brutal arena combat, character progression, and strategic city management creates a gameplay loop that remains compelling across long campaigns. The constant risk of losing valuable fighters ensures that every battle feels meaningful, while the evolving roster of gladiators and enemies keeps the tactical challenges fresh. For fans of turn-based strategy games that emphasize careful planning and high-stakes decision making, Bloodgrounds offers a rich and rewarding experience. By combining elements of gladiatorial spectacle with thoughtful tactical gameplay, the game captures the thrill of survival in a brutal arena where only the strongest—and the most strategic—can rise to glory. Rating: 8/10

Promising, but feels undercooked. There's a lot to like about Bloodgrounds. The visuals are very clean, there's a variety of actions and skills, the town upgrades feel meaningful, and gear is just complicated enough to be interesting without feeling like a distraction from your teamplay. The problems come in with the central gameplay activity of the game: the arena combat. This is really let down by a few leading things. First and not entirely a complaint, permadeath is tolerable in a game like this, but I could see it frustrating some people. Given how enemy action economy works, it's entirely possible for a gladiator to get dogpiled with damage and negative effects and so killed very quickly. This doesn't bother me too much, but can feel a bit cheap to lose a unit because the enemy team had a lot of mobility to let it focus fire someone and there was little you could do about it. Far more frustrating is the Trauma system, which applies semi-permanent debuffs like halved movement or reduced damage. These can be removed between fights by having character rest at the infirmary for a round. The problem is that you get them faster than you can remove them. Full health character gets crit by a weak attack? Immediate trauma. You'll have characters coming out of fights taking barely chip damage with a couple of traumas because of how freely these are handed out. And they last for all the fights that day, meaning a trash enemy in the first fight can saddle your best unit with crippling debuffs for multiple fights in a row, all because you allowed a ranged enemy to attack your armored fighter a single time. And there are multiple ways to get these, so it is not uncommon to see 1-3 on every character on your team even after some easy fights. Another source of traumas is the Entertainment system. A lot of gladiator games have these; rewards for aggression, for using certain weapons, or raw brutality. Here, the list of actions is partly random, and frequently remind you this is a video game. Imagine being punished for making attacks. That's right, people don't come to this arena to see people stab each other. Amazing. You can lose entertainment for every attack you make, while getting rewarded for stalling a match out 5 or more rounds LONGER by avoiding enemies so you can spam healing in a corner. Or avoid doing damage while you stack a status effect. If your entertainment is too low, you can get more traumas from that. Incredible. The entertainment system is a good idea, but needs work. Less rewards for stalling and corner camping, and more rewards that tie into aggression or engaging the enemy. Quests that MANDATE stalling, like healing an amount that requires 5+ rounds of avoiding combat, or collecting a number of trophies that simply don't drop regularly, should be reduced or removed. Overall, it just feels janky and gamey in combat, rather than even vaguely immersive or tactical. Fights turn into a boring trudge of pursuing mini-rewards because these pay far more than winning the fights themselves.

Tactical games are my jam. I love games that allows me to build and grow a mercenary company the way I see fit, so this title was very appealing to me. After playing for a while, I grew bored very quickly. You see the game pits your gladiator in a 11x11 square with random, theme appropriate ennemies and RANDOM amounts of traps/terrain. So you don't get a challenging encounter has been finely tuned for your level. No, you get a random chaotic mess where strategy and tactics is irrelevant. Let me give you an example: I spawn into an arena. 80% of the squares are fill with wall, statues, traps, etc.. There's a 'saw trap' that runs all along the arena for absurd amount of damage. Looking at how little I can move around the free squares that are left, I figure it's better to turtle in my starting position around my flag (gives armor every round) and wait for the enemy to come to me. I skipped 25 turns, the enemy never got to me and they all died from traps trying to get to me. The game is mostly fine for the first arena, but the further you get, the more egregious the trap ammount and lethality gets. It's not that it's hard, it's just tedious and unfun. Especially since your characters cannot go through friendlies, you often cannot act because there's just no space to go around. Most abilities won't allow you to target through your allies either, so trying to line up your characters to: 1: hit the ennemies 2: not be in the pathway of any kind of traps 3: be in a spot that won't get your character killed (permadeath btw) Is really difficult. Most fights I just sit in a corner around my flag and healing spirit and wait. Nuke one target at a time as they come, repeat ad nauseam. Also, the UI is terrible. It's a 3/4 locked view. So in order to target the square next to your character, you need to click through your model. The problem is the cursor detection is very imprecise. I would hold the cursor over the left square but the ability icon would show it on the bottom square. Just imagine having a box in front of your character, the game has to 'see through' the box, your character model, your other character model that's kinda in the way AND target the proper square behind all this. It slows down the pace considerably becaue you can't act quick when the UI is not responsive. My suggestion for this would be to allow top down view to easily target the squares you want. In resume: Good concept but arena repetitiveness, bad AI/UI and limited movement options makes it a game you'll grow bored in around 10 hours.

This is an absolute gem of a game (with a few flaws). Pros: + The unique, fresh setting of historical gladiatorial battles mixed with fantasy elements (i.e. creatures and magic) + The tactical combat is very satisfying with tons of options (fighter positioning, arena traps and arena-specific conditions, your own traps and machinery, equipment-specific abilities, etc.) + The multi-layered meta-game, with base building, fighter recruiting with RPG elements / cosmetic tuning / traumas / perma-death / etc. + Presentation. From the menu art and general UI which are very intuitive to the actual combat which comprises of a pleasant-looking, pixelated 3D arena and character models. To be noted, the arena view can be rotated so that you can see / target those hard to see, obscured tiles + Customizable keys. So many games nowadays are sold without this basic quality of life feature + Excellent replayability tanks to the number of fighter classes, equipment and arenas randomization = Ridiculous people with ~10h of gameplay who complain about enemies targeting your weakest fighters while this is (and should be) your own strategy are, well, ridiculous and should be ignored = Also, to rectify another piece of their disinformation, your fighters cannot receives traumas from regular attacks, only from critical hits Cons: - You cannot save mid-battle. Once you commit to a tournament you have to finish it one way or the other; this does not respect the gamer's time. The dev's given reason is that they do not want the system to be 'abused' via save-scumming. In a single-player game. In 2026. - No [i]undo[/i] option during battles. You have mis-clicked targeting an enemy on a crowded area or when moving, that's it, it's final, no way to correct that - Pathfinding. If there are multiple routes, for the same number of steps, for your fighter to get somewhere with or without entering an enemy's zone of control / trap, the default option will always take you through the enemy's ZOC / trap thus receiving unnecessary, avoidable damage - Something's not quite right with the evade percentages (e.g. I've had enemies with less than 10% evade chance dodge multiple times in a row, particularly so when they're about to die) - Music and story are nothing special but do a decent job to support the overall experience and game progression - Technically speaking the game runs fine on my desktop PC, but on my laptop the game fails to remember the set resolution which has to be re-adjusted each new session

I finally beat it! Man, was not expecting that long of a playthrough. First just want to state, this game isn't easy. I played on medium difficulty, and it took me quite a bit to get through everything. Judging based on the % of ppl who have achievements I can say a couple things. 1, do not be afraid to lose gladiators. They will come and they definitely will go. Also, you can utilize high level ones that died once you get a memorial. 2, people are clearly not getting very far and putting this one down due to difficulty? or the time it takes to get through. That is understandable, but that doesn't mean it should have a negative review, as you can play on a lower difficulty. This game can lead to some frustrating outcomes, but I never wanted to put it down for good until I saw it all the way through. Things I liked: The core tactic play was good. The variety of the spells and gladiator types was good. The armor and how it changed the way your character looked was good. The players almost had an old mortal kombat feel to them. Building up the base was fun. The colosseum you can build for duels was more fun than I expected. The shorter duels vs standard enemies was a nice switch up between the long challenges. I thought the story was decent, and I'm guessing you can have different endings based on some of your choices. I didn't witness any bugs which was nice. If I was to caption it, I would say this is a gladiator version of darkest dungeon. Games are completely different, but the harsh run throughs, and the slow build up to finally finishing off the bosses has that same feel. Things I did not like: The traumas. This needs to be adjusted. A random crit that does little to no damage putting a heavy negative perm. buff on a unit for the rest of the challenge, is a little too harsh in my opinion. Music. I'm not sure why, but the music drove me crazy. I think because it is simple and repeats constantly. I ended up turning the music down, and just played some youtube videos on the side. The overall cost of things needs to be toned way down, or the amount of money given needs to be updated. The spell upgrades cost too much, the building upgrades cost too much. Healing units cost too much. It can feel frustrating to feel the need to not try for the next harder step up because you feel like you should grind an easier mode to get money. A couple times would be fine, but between all the things you have to spend on, it feels like an extremely long grind. I chose not to, and continued to push on without all the upgrades possible for a section, and I am glad I did. The only time I felt like the money was given appropriately was the last place. Here it would give you enough to level a base and some extra spending money, but by then it was too late, and I didn't even need to upgrade everything. Summary I think it was well made, fun, at times a bit too grindy, harsh in a good way, turn based game that deserves a checkout if you like a challenge.

Pros - A solid variety of weapons, builds and weapons available. Whether you want to go in for single target DPS, stun with a hammer/long range support with spells or bows/javelins there's tons of variety anda potential here. - Somewhat interesting story and there is some replayability (just as well since I cleared the game just shy of 24 hours, tbf I did import my save from the demo after clearing the first Act). Cons - Music is a bit too repetitive for my tastes, especially for a 20+ hour RPG. - Lategame frustration with status effects, in particular stun effects should have been more limited. - Polarising difficulty. I was able to breeze through normal with minimal issues but the hardest mode felt more focused on punishment than optimised strategy. - Length felt just a little short. Despite taking my time with extra arena battles and some achievement hunting, a SRPG vet could finish this in 20 hours or under so I just wish there was some more things to do after the game is cleared, maybe some postgame boss battles or challenge missions. - AI's intelligence is rather lacking. Quite a few times it would focus on destroying traps instead of damaging my gladiators which seems like a pretty big oversight. - An item filter would have been very useful. By midgame I was just selling a lot of my unused gear because it was too much of a timewaster to sort through lesser gear. - I wish recruiting gladiators was easier. Of the many missions and arena battles the chances of them surrending feels absurdly low, to the point of not wanting to bother after a while. Also on that point, kind of wish the arena battles were more challenging as they don't give them good gear leading to very fast clears. tl;dr A great game with a couple of flaws but well worth a look if you like strategy RPG's and a somewhat unique setting. Would be very interested in a sequel or extra content to clear as it has massive potential. Pick it up on sale, it's good value!

The only negative thing I can say is that you have to equip and re-equip your guys before every session, and without any equipment management it gets boring real fast, you have to scroll through the pile of ever growing equip a lot, comparing stats.
